title: Local Plan Viability Study
description:
Newcastle-under-Lyme Borough Council (NuLBC) is currently preparing its new Local Plan. Work on the Local Plan commenced in January 2021 and to date has included public consultation on Issues and Strategic Options in late 2021 and early 2022 and the First Draft Local Plan in July and August 2023. The Borough Council is seeking to commission a consultant to update a Plan wide Viability Study of the Local Plan, policies and allocations.
The NuLBC First Draft Local Plan (2023) contained a suite of policies and proposed allocations as part of the consultation document. The Council also consulted on three strategic locations, these were sites of scale in the Green Belt where the Council has sought views on the principle of large scale strategic locations but has not given a view on their suitability. The locations of the three strategic locations are at J16 of the M6, one located at Talke and another at Keele. A copy of the First Draft Local Plan can be viewed here:- First Draft Local Plan 2020-2040 - Keystone (newcastle-staffs.gov.uk).
The study area is the Newcastle-under-Lyme Borough Council administrative area. The evidence base in support of the First Draft Local Plan is published on the Borough Council website: - Local plan evidence base - Newcastle-under-Lyme Borough Council (newcastle-staffs.gov.uk) and includes the Local Plan Viability Study (2023) that supported the First Draft Local Plan. The new / updated viability study is expected to make reference to the 2023 Local Plan viability study for context and should be informed by comments made to the First Draft Local Plan, with relevance to viability. The next iteration of the Local Plan will be the final draft version of the Local Plan (at Regulation 19 stage).

description:
The provision of a haulage service to transfer the following waste streams to the Treatment Facilities identified:

1. Staffordshire Moorlands District Council (SMDC) Waste from Leek Transfer Station, Fowlchurch Road, Ball Haye Green, Leek, ST13 6BH

a) SMDC Kerbside collected Household Waste transferred to Stoke Waste to Energy Plant, Campbell Road, Stoke on Trent ST4 4DX,

b) SMDC Kerbside collected Household Waste transferred to Veolia ES Staffordshire, Enterprise Drive, Four Ashes, Wolverhampton, WV10 7DF

c) SMDC Kerbside collected Household Waste transferred to Biffa Waste Services, Poplars Landfill, Lichfield Road, Cannock, WS11 8NQ

d) SMDC Street Cleaning Residues transferred to Biffa Aggregate Treatment and Recycling Facility (ATRF), Meece Landfill, Blackflats Road, Swynnerton, Nr Stone, ST15 0QN

2 Staffordshire County Council (SCC) Street Cleaning Residues from Stone Household Waste Recycling Centre (HWRC), Stone Business Park, Beacon Rd, Stone ST15 0NN to Biffa ATRF, Meece Landfill, Blackflats Road, Swynnerton, Nr Stone, ST15 0QN

title: Astley Centre Fit-Out Project
description:
The Borough Council is working with an innovative designer on an interim venue to be used to generate awareness of a local Newcastle-under-Lyme hero Philip Astley and celebrate his life and contribution to the modern day circus.
The centre is intended to appeal to everyone, from young children to older adults.
It will be used by the general public, school groups, community groups and for education and outreach.
The centre will display permanent exhibits relating to Philip Astley, his contribution to circus and also celebrate the wider circus landscape. It will display various temporary exhibits over the year, which may include performance elements.
It will be a multi use centre, accommodating educational talks, screenings, outreach programmes and be available for other uses generating income for the Borough Council.
The venue identified for the interim use is 23-25 Merrial Street, Newcastle-under-Lyme, ST5 2AD which is currently a dilapidated property.
Refurbishment of this property has commenced by other parties. This will enable the themed fit-out to follow. The successful bidder will have full access to all refurbishment drawings. They will be able to liaise with the refurbishment design team and contractor during the refurbishment period.

title: Occupational Health Services
description:
The Borough Council of Newcastle-under-Lyme are looking to procure the provision of Occupational Health Services.
Principal Requirements include:
> Provision of advice and guidance on best practice relating to relevant occupational health matters proactively and professionally including Health and Safety considerations.
> Provision of high quality, and timely support, advice and guidance in response to individual occupational issues with possible health and safety implications.
> Maintenance, review and updating of confidential health records in accordance with agreed principles and the requirements of Equalities Act, GDPR, Human Rights Act (HRA) and Freedom of Information Act (FOI).  It must be ensured that effective business continuity measures are in place to protect and preserve records.
> Compiling and analysing statistical information to identify trends and propose areas for further action including DNA rates and repeat appointments.
> Ensure effective consultation and communication with the Council.
> Provision of timely and accurate management information with clear and accessible management advice.
> Provision of efficient timely administrative support for occupational health services.
> Documentation must be standard across the Council.
> Relevant management reports to be communicated directly with the referring manager through mutually agreed means. Advice on proactive approach to managing attendance.
> To support the client in effective management of employees by supplying accurate assessments and sound advice to the employer primarily to enable managers to make timely and appropriate decisions concerning the future employment relationship.
> Provision of support and training information to managers on handling health matters with individuals and groups.
> Timely and effective completion of pre-employment checks and where applicable immunisations.

title: Authority wide design code
description:
The Council has been successful in being selected as one of the Government's pathfinder areas for the production of design codes.\r
\r
The Council are in the process of preparing a new Local Plan. This will replace the current adopted Newcastle-Under-Lyme and Stoke-on-Trent Joint Core Spatial Strategy, 2009 and the saved policies from the Stoke-on-Trent City Plan 2001.\r
\r
The Council wishes to commission the production of a design code which will be referenced in the new Local Plan.\r
\r
The Council's development plan is the Core Spatial Strategy 2009 and has also in place a Supplementary Planning Document - Newcastle-under-Lyme and Stoke-on-Trent Urban Design Guidance (2010) and a Supplementary Planning Document - Inclusive Design Access for All (2008). These provide design guidance for the city. Heritage and culture is an important characteristic for the city.\r
\r
The Government attaches increasing importance to design reflected through the Levelling Up and Regeneration Act 2023 and the introduction of the National Model for Design Codes. The Council wants to encourage high-quality design and to make the planning process easier for applicants in respect of design considerations.

Staffordshire County Council's Community Learning Service wishes to commission a Community Learning Framework.

title: IA2777 Supportive Communities Citizen Inquiry Programme- Health and Wellbeing
description:
Staffordshire County Council (SCC) would like to hear from Providers who have the skills and knowledge to deliver a Citizens Inquiry Programme to support the work of Supportive Communities team, Public Health.
      
      The aim of the Programme is to create the conditions to engage, involve and empower communities to understand, prioritise and co-produce solutions to address 'what communities and organisations can do together to help people be healthy and sustain positive wellbeing'.  To provide qualitative insight to work with citizens to identify the root causes of Health Inequalities which drives poor health and wellbeing in certain populations, which in turn, can lead to an increased demand for adult Social care services.
      
      The outcomes of the Programme will support the aims and objectives of Supportive Communities working with our Community Champions programme.   
      
      The COVID-19 pandemic has placed an even greater emphasis on the benefits of living healthier lives.  The Citizen's Inquiry will consist of 4 phases:
      
      Phase one - Citizen's Inquiry sessions
      Phase two - Commentator sessions
      Phase three - Community Led research
      Phase four - Recommendations and report
      
      There are two Lots. Potential Providers can bid for one or both Lots:
      •	Newcastle Under Lyme (Lot One)
      •	Tamworth (Lot Two)
      
      SCC will purchase one Programme per lot.

title: Green Infrastructure Mapping Database. Urban Habitat and Naturalness Mapping Phase 3
description:
An Earth Observation based approach to developing Urban Habitat and Naturalness Maps was developed during 2021/22 and further refined during 2022/23 which included the upscaling of application of the method to a small selection of major urban conurbations in England (Tyneside, Greater Manchester, Greater Birmingham). 
In upscaling (known as the Phase 1 roll out), the Urban Habitat and Naturalness method was refined to a point where it is intended that no further refinements will be made so as to ensure that a suite of maps for all the major urban conurbations in England can be developed with a consistent method underpinning their development. Subsequent methodological modifications may then be made to create an updated method for use in developing any second iteration Urban Habitat and Naturalness Maps in the future. 

The focus of this contract will be on applying the established method to a third phase suite of areas in order to expand the England coverage of Urban Habitat and Naturalness maps. The target areas for Phase 3 of the Urban Habitat and Naturalness mapping are the East Midlands including Nottingham, Derby and Leicester, Teesside, Coventry, Stoke and Newcastle under Lyme, Dartford and Gravesham, Sheffield and Rotherham. The contact will apply the mapping method to the target areas and deliver a suite of GIS based whole area maps of Broad and Detailed Urban Habitats, Naturalness and Combined Naturalness Factor maps for publicly accessible green spaces. The mapping will cover the area within the combined administrative boundaries of the local authorities within the target areas.

title: Improving the Emotional Health and Wellbeing for Children and Young People in Staffordshire
description:
Staffordshire's County Council and Clinical Commissioning Groups have a shared vision for the development of emotional health and wellbeing services for children and young people in Staffordshire.  This is based on the principles of Thrive and gives emphasis to a preventative, early intervention approach.  The vision is ambitious and aims to deliver an accessible and responsive service to the children and young people of our county.

Staffordshire covers a large geographical area and is divided into the eight (8) districts of Cannock Chase, East Staffordshire, Lichfield, Newcastle-under-Lyme, South Staffordshire, Stafford, Staffordshire Moorlands and Tamworth.

Service aims are:
•	To promote positive emotional health and wellbeing, whilst offering a self-help and face to face support system to those who require it;
•	To enable children and young people to access services at a time and level they feel is appropriate for them;
•	Build resilience in individuals, peer groups, family units and communities;
•	To be inclusive of the Looked After Children and Care Leaver cohort within Staffordshire;
•	Reduce the prevalence of escalating emotional health and wellbeing issues for children and young people, through prevention and early intervention;
•	To work collaboratively with professionals, families and services utilising local/place-based arrangements to ensure a child centred approach to support is a reality, not an aspiration.

The Service will offer a flexible approach to meeting the needs of Children and Young People (CYP) aged 5-18, who have mild to moderate mental health needs.  The offer will be one that is made up of following;

•	Preventative Work
o	Low level information, advice and guidance
o	Peer support
o	Raising awareness of emotional health and wellbeing issues within communities, families, peer groups and with individuals
o	Tackling the stigma around mental and emotional health
o	Promotion of new, future emotional health and wellbeing services whilst utilising existing statutory services that support CYP and families in a variety of ways.
o	Effective work with stakeholders to ensure cohesive services

•	Self-Help via Digital Support 
o	 Support for young people
o	 Self-referral service
o	 Online counselling.  

•	Direct Support
o	 Therapeutic offer 
o	 Wide range of therapies
o	 Group support
o	 1:1 support
o	 Peer support 

The tender will be procured via a Competitive Dialogue tender process. This will be a three-stage process: -
1.	Submission of Selection Questionnaire 
2.	Invitation to Participate in Dialogue 
3.	Invitation to Submit Final Bid - Invitation to tender

Suppliers should register on the Proactis e-tendering system: https://supplierlive.proactisp2p.com and then select this tender opportunity to view and return tender documents.
